senses.en: fall in drops
examples: She was hot and sweat [[dripped]] into her eyes.
Her boots were muddy and her hair was [[dripping]].

senses.en: let liquid fall in drops
examples: She was hot and sweat [[dripped]] into her eyes.
Her boots were muddy and her hair was [[dripping]].

senses.en: breathless
examples: She had a car accident and suffered a [[breathtaking]] pain.
The view from my bedroom window was absolutely [[breathtaking]].

senses.zh: 激动人心的；惊人的；令人惊叹的
senses.en: very impressive, exciting, or surprising
examples: She had a car accident and suffered a [[breathtaking]] pain.
The view from my bedroom window was absolutely [[breathtaking]].

senses.en: (BrE fulfilment) the feeling of being happy and satisfied with your life because you are doing interesting, useful, or important things
examples: Are you looking for greater [[fulfillment]] and satisfaction in your work?

senses.en: very happy, or likely to make people very happy
examples: It was a [[joyful]] reunion of all the family.

senses.en: (fml.) similar and happening at the same time
examples: Social changes in Britain are matched by [[parallel]] trends in some other countries.
The railway is [[parallel]] with the canal.

senses.en: two lines, paths, etc. that are parallel to each other are the same distance apart along their whole length
examples: Social changes in Britain are matched by [[parallel]] trends in some other countries.
The railway is [[parallel]] with the canal.

senses.en: (fml.) bigger, better, or worse than anything else
examples: They enjoyed success on a scale [[unparalleled]] by any previous pop group.

senses.zh: 伤人的；不顾他人感受的
senses.en: not pleasant and not sensitive to people's feelings
examples: She spoke with [[brutal]] honesty — I was too old for the job.
Jensen is a dangerous man, and can be very [[brutal]] and reckless (不顾后果的).

senses.en: very cruel and violent
examples: She spoke with [[brutal]] honesty — I was too old for the job.
Jensen is a dangerous man, and can be very [[brutal]] and reckless (不顾后果的).

senses.en: the quality of being honest
examples: She answered all my questions with her usual [[honesty]].

senses.zh: 难以忍受的；承受不住的；无法容忍的
senses.en: too unpleasant, painful, or annoying to deal with
examples: The atmosphere at work at the moment is quite [[unbearable]].

senses.zh: 戏弄；逗弄；拿···取笑（开玩笑）
senses.en: laugh at sb. and make jokes in order to have fun by embarrassing them, either in a friendly way or in an unkind way
examples: I used to hate being [[teased]] about my red hair when I was at school.

senses.en: try to make sb. angry or upset by saying unkind things to them
examples: It's wrong for you to [[taunt]] him because of his size.

senses.en: make sb. want to have or do sth., even though they know they really should not
examples: Don't [[tempt]] thieves by leaving valuables clearly visible.
They [[tempted]] him to join the company by offering him a large salary and a company car.

senses.en: try to persuade sb. to do sth. by making it seem attractive
examples: Don't [[tempt]] thieves by leaving valuables clearly visible.
They [[tempted]] him to join the company by offering him a large salary and a company car.

senses.en: always supporting your friends, principles, country, etc.
examples: Jack has been a [[loyal]] worker in this company for almost 50 years.

senses.en: (usu. in negatives) stop yourself from having sth. that you like very much or doing sth. that you want to do
examples: He was unable to [[resist]] the temptation to buy the wallet.

senses.en: the act of celebrating
examples: This was not a memorial service but a [[celebration]] of his life.
There were wild street [[celebrations]] when England won the Cup.

senses.en: an occasion or party when you celebrate sth.
examples: This was not a memorial service but a [[celebration]] of his life.
There were wild street [[celebrations]] when England won the Cup.

senses.en: used to say that people or things do sth. or exist together at the same time
examples: Most of the staff refused to work [[alongside]] the new team.
He crossed the street and walked [[alongside]] the park.

senses.en: next to the side of sth.
examples: Most of the staff refused to work [[alongside]] the new team.
He crossed the street and walked [[alongside]] the park.

senses.en: an inability to stop doing or using sth., esp. sth. harmful
examples: He is now fighting his [[addiction]] to alcohol.

senses.en: a pleasant activity
examples: After a long day of work, I found boating a [[distraction]].
I study in the library as there are too many [[distractions]] at home.

senses.en: sth. that stops you paying attention to what you are doing
examples: After a long day of work, I found boating a [[distraction]].
I study in the library as there are too many [[distractions]] at home.

senses.en: the colored part of the sky where the sun is appearing in the morning
examples: There was a glorious [[sunrise]] over the mountains.
They went out at [[sunrise]] to go bird-watching.

senses.en: the time when the sun first appears in the morning
examples: There was a glorious [[sunrise]] over the mountains.
They went out at [[sunrise]] to go bird-watching.

senses.zh: 有礼貌地，仁慈地，和蔼地，亲切地（尤指对较低阶层的人们）
senses.en: in a polite, kind, and generous way, esp. to people of a lower rank
examples: Mr. Martel [[graciously]] agreed to take time out of his busy schedule to answer some questions.

senses.en: make sb. lose their physical strength, or become physically weak
examples: Elsa was [[weakened]] by her long illness.
The new evidence [[weakens]] the case against her.

senses.en: make sb. / sth. less powerful or less important, or become less powerful
examples: Elsa was [[weakened]] by her long illness.
The new evidence [[weakens]] the case against her.

senses.en: a small raised area on a surface
examples: Her bicycle hit a [[bump]] in the road and threw her off.
Tim was a clumsy boy, always [[bumping]] into the furniture.

senses.en: hit or knock against sth.
examples: Her bicycle hit a [[bump]] in the road and threw her off.
Tim was a clumsy boy, always [[bumping]] into the furniture.

senses.en: show or say that sth. will happen in the future
examples: The storms of that year [[foreshadowed]] a long period of unstable weather conditions.

senses.en: (~s) the area just outside the lines that form the edge of a sports field
examples: Wenger stood on the [[sidelines]] shouting instructions to his team.
Jim works in a bank, but teaches French in the evenings as a [[sideline]].

senses.en: an activity that you do as well as your main job or business, in order to earn more money
examples: Wenger stood on the [[sidelines]] shouting instructions to his team.
Jim works in a bank, but teaches French in the evenings as a [[sideline]].

senses.en: always, or for a very long time
examples: Michael and his family have settled [[permanently]] in the States.

senses.en: (always + ad. / prep.) move back and away from sth., esp. because you are frightened
examples: His anger was enough to make the others [[shrink away]] from him.
Your sweater will [[shrink]] if you wash it at too high a temperature.

senses.en: become smaller, or make sth. smaller, through the effects of heat or water
examples: His anger was enough to make the others [[shrink away]] from him.
Your sweater will [[shrink]] if you wash it at too high a temperature.

senses.en: try to deal with a difficult problem
examples: There is more than one way to [[tackle]] the problem.

senses.en: the possibility that sth. will happen
examples: There is every [[prospect]] of the weather remaining dry this week.

senses.en: a bend in a road, river, etc.
examples: As he rounded the [[curve]] he saw her standing by the gate.
The seats were arranged to form a [[curve]].

senses.en: a line that gradually bends like part of a circle
examples: As he rounded the [[curve]] he saw her standing by the gate.
The seats were arranged to form a [[curve]].

senses.zh: （跨栏赛跑或马术比赛中用的）栏架
senses.en: one of a series of small fences that a person or horse has to jump over during a race
examples: She cleared all the [[hurdles]] easily and raced to the finishing line.
Finding enough money for the project was the first [[hurdle]].

senses.en: a problem or difficulty that you must deal with before you can achieve sth.
examples: She cleared all the [[hurdles]] easily and raced to the finishing line.
Finding enough money for the project was the first [[hurdle]].

senses.zh: 离婚，分手（尤作报刊用语）
senses.en: (infml.) the end of a marriage or relationship — used esp. in newspapers and magazines
examples: She seems to be getting over her recent [[split]] with her fiancé.
The party is [[split]] over the issue of immigration.

senses.en: (split, split) divide, or make a group of people divide, into smaller groups that have very different opinions
examples: She seems to be getting over her recent [[split]] with her fiancé.
The party is [[split]] over the issue of immigration.

senses.en: break or make sth. break, either so that it gets lines on its surface, or so that it breaks into pieces
examples: Due to her carelessness, she fell and [[cracked]] a bone in her leg.

senses.en: having one or more lines on the surface because it is damaged but not completely broken
examples: She passed her tongue over her [[cracked]] lips and tried to speak.

senses.en: if you do sth. by choice, you do it because you want to do it and not because you are forced to do it
examples: She repeated that she was very comfortable and lived here [[by choice]].

senses.en: for only sb. to have or use; not shared
examples: I'm going out, so you'll have the place [[to yourself]].

senses.en: use all of sth. and not have any more left
examples: Few of us would know what to do if the supermarkets [[ran out of]] food.
We must act now because time is [[running out]].

senses.en: (of a supply of sth.) be used up
examples: Few of us would know what to do if the supermarkets [[ran out of]] food.
We must act now because time is [[running out]].

senses.en: (also be sick to death of) (spoken) be angry or bored with sth. that has been happening for a long time
examples: I'm [[sick of]] your rudeness — I won't have it any longer!

senses.zh: 向（某人）发泄（不满等）；拿（某人）出气
senses.en: treat sb. badly when you are angry or upset, even though it is not their fault
examples: When he's under pressure at work, he [[takes it out on]] me.

senses.zh: 前进中的问题（通常是暂时的）
senses.en: (infml.) a problem that arises and interferes with forward progress (usu. only temporarily)
examples: The project hit [[a bump in the road]] when Tom suddenly resigned.

senses.en: start doing or discussing sth. new
examples: When you finish, [[move on]] to the next exercise.

senses.en: be able to do what you need to do, earn your own money, etc. without help from others
examples: Jack's never learned to [[stand on his own two feet]].
